name: figma-offset-centred-endboard
exporter: Figma - Export > SVG, Include "id" attribute ON, Outline text OFF
story: A student show's endboard: a nearly full-width plate with both lines composed over its left side, because the right third is empty on purpose.
idioms: text-anchor="middle" on both <text>, with the tspan's x at the centre of the LINE (x="700")
that stated centre 260 units left of the plate's own midline (x=960), which is the composition rather than a mistake
the frame contents inside <g clip-path="url(#clipN)"> with the matching <defs><clipPath>
letter-spacing in em including a negative one on the display line, family names without a face suffix
xml:space="preserve" plus style="white-space: pre", fractional baselines
whyThisMatters: Every other centre-anchored file in the corpus is drawn ON the middle of its box, so the anchor the exporter states and the placement the drawing shows agree and nothing tells them apart. Here they disagree, which is the ordinary case of a designer using negative space: the anchor says a longer value grows both ways, the drawing says it grows both ways FROM x=700. Read as a request to be centred in the plate, the lines jump 260 units right the first time an operator types. Read as a start-anchored line - which is what a missing anchor would mean here - a long value fills rightwards from x=700 out to the plate's far margin and paints 90 units off the plate's LEFT edge, because centre-anchored text spends half its width on each side. Both are visible the moment somebody types, and neither is visible at the length the designer drew.
